result.topic_en: Calculations toward the theory of the Nobili colour rings: reducing integrals of the form $\int e^{-n\pi t/2x}(t^2-r^2)^{-1/2}dt$ to hypergeometric-type integrals via a Möbius substitution, relations among the integrals over different intervals (with sine coefficients), and a Bessel-type series expansion.
result.transcription:
Zu Theorie der Nobili'schen Farbenringe.
$\int_r^\infty \frac{e^{-n\frac{\pi}{2x}t}\,\partial t}{\sqrt{t^2-r^2}} =$
$\int (x-a)^\alpha (x-b)^\beta (x-c)^\gamma (x-\partial)^\delta \partial x \quad \alpha+\beta+\gamma+\delta=-2$
$y = \frac{x-b}{x-a}\cdot\frac{c-a}{c-b}$
$z = \frac{\partial-a}{\partial-b}\cdot\frac{c-b}{c-a}$
$x=a \quad \infty \quad 0$
$x=b \quad 0 \quad 1 \quad \infty$
$x=c \quad 1 \quad 0 \quad \infty$
$x=\partial \quad \infty \quad 1 \quad 0$
$x-b = y\,(x-a)\frac{c-b}{c-a}$
$x-c = (1-y)\frac{b-c}{b-a}(x-a)$
$x-\partial = (1-zy)\frac{b-\partial}{b-a}(x-a)$
$z(x-a)\frac{c-b}{c-a} - (x-b)$
$= \frac{a-b}{c-a}(x-c)$
$= (x-a)\frac{c-b}{c-a}(1-y)$
$A = \int_0^1 y^\beta (1-y)^\gamma (1-zy)^\delta \partial y$
$B = \int_0^1 y^\delta (1-y)^\beta (1-zy)^\alpha \partial y$
$y + \frac{1-y}{1-zy}$
$1-y + \frac{y(1-z)}{1-zy}$
$1-zy + \frac{(1-z)}{1-zy}$
$A = (1-z)^{\gamma+\delta+1} B = (1-z)^{-\alpha-\beta-1} B$
$\int_0^1 y^\beta (1-y)^\gamma (1-zy)^\delta \partial y$
$-\infty \quad A \quad 0 \quad B \quad 1 \quad C \quad \frac{1}{z} \quad D \quad \infty$
$e^{\beta\pi i}$
$\sin s\,A + \sin(\beta\pi+s)\,B + \sin((\beta+\gamma)\pi+s)\,C + \sin((\beta+\gamma+\delta)\pi+s)\,D$
$= 0$
$(1-\frac{z}{n}y)^n = e^{n\log(1-\frac{z}{n}y)} = e^{-zy}$
$\sin\alpha\pi\,A + \sin(\alpha+\beta)\pi\,B + \sin\delta\pi\,C = 0$
$\sin(\alpha+\delta)\pi\,A + \sin\gamma\pi\,B + \sin\delta\pi\,D$
$D = \left([-\sin\alpha\pi-]\frac{\partial A}{\partial\delta}\sin(\alpha+\gamma\pi) - \sin\gamma\pi\frac{\partial B}{\partial\delta}\right)\frac{1}{\pi\cos\delta\pi}$
$C = \left(\sin\alpha\pi\frac{\partial A}{\partial\delta} + \sin(\alpha+\beta)\pi\frac{\partial B}{\partial\delta}\right)\frac{1}{\pi\cos\delta\pi}$
$\sin\beta\pi\,B + \sin(\beta+\gamma)\pi\,C + \sin[-...-](\beta+\gamma+\delta)\pi\,D$
$\int (t+r)^{-\frac12}(t-r)^{-\frac12}\partial t$
$e^{\mu\pi i}$
$\int_{-r}^{r} e^{-n\frac{\pi}{2x}t}(t+r)^\mu (t-r)^\nu \partial t = A$
$\int_r^\infty e^{\cdot}(t+r)^\mu (r-t)^\nu \partial t = B$
$(e^{\mu\pi i} - e^{-\mu\pi i})A +$
$\int \frac{e^{-zt}(1-t)^{-\frac12}\log t\,\partial t}{}$
$\frac{\partial^2 b_n}{\partial r^2} + \frac{1}{r}\frac{\partial b_n}{\partial r} + nn\,b_n = 0$
$\int_{-r}^{r} e^{-nt}(r^2-t^2)^{-\frac12}\partial t = \pi\cdot\sum\frac{(-nr)^{2m}}{\Pi(m)^2}$
$= \int_{-1}^{1} e^{-nrt}(1-t^2)^{-\frac12}\partial t$
$= \sum\int_{-1}^{1}\frac{(-nrt)^m}{\Pi m}(1-t^2)^{-\frac12}\partial t$
$= 2\sum\int_0^1 t^{2m}(1-t^2)^{-\frac12}\partial t \qquad \frac{(-nr)^{2m}}{\Pi 2m}$
$\sum\int_0^1 t^{(m-\frac12)}(1-t)^{-\frac12}\partial t$
$\sum\frac{\Pi(m-\frac12)\,\Pi(-\frac12)}{\Pi m\,\Pi 2m}(-nr)^{2m}$
$(\Pi-\frac12)^2\sum\frac{(-nr)^{2m}}{\Pi m\,2^{2m}\ldots(2m-1)} \quad 2m-2$
$\Pi 2m = 2^{2m}\,\Pi m\cdot\frac{\Pi(m-\frac12)}{\Pi(-\frac12)}$
$\int_0^1 t^{-\frac12}(1-t)^{-\frac12}\partial t = 2\cdot\frac{\pi}{2}$
$\int_{-r}^{r} e^{-nt}(r-t)^\beta (t+r)^\alpha \partial t = A$
$\alpha+\beta=-2$
$\int_r^\infty e^{-nt}(t-r)^\beta (t+r)^\alpha \partial t = B$
$-1-\alpha$
$A\sin\alpha\pi + B\sin(\alpha+\beta)\pi = C$
$B = \frac{C - A\sin\alpha\pi}{\sin(\alpha+\beta)\pi} \qquad B\ \frac{\partial C}{\partial\beta} - \frac{\partial A}{}$

methods.what: Möbius substitution mapping the four singular points a,b,c,d of the integrand to 0,1,∞,1/z, reducing it to a hypergeometric (Euler-type) integral
Euler integral representations of two branches over (0,1)
Transformation relating the two integrals by a power of (1-z)
Cauchy contour linear relation among integrals over the four intervals with sine coefficients
Degenerate case: differentiating with respect to the exponent to obtain C and D
Bessel differential equation of order zero
Series expansion of the integral (Bessel I0 type) by termwise integration using Beta integrals
Duplication formula for the factorial (Gauss Π) function
Linear relation between the integrals over (-r,r) and (r,∞) with exponential kernel
